managers.message_to_team: The memo says notes are expected on every cup while we’re off-peak, so please add a quick mark to each one today. If we get six or more waiting or we’re short-staffed, skip it and keep the window moving.
managers.private_thought: With the line this short and staffing on plan, there’s no reason we shouldn’t meet the audit expectation without letting it slow the drive-thru.

managers.message_to_team: Mid-morning is quiet enough, so put any quick mark on each cup—smiley, heart, whatever—and I’ll check a few. If we hit six waiting or we’re short-staffed, keep the line moving and skip it.
managers.private_thought: It’s a small labor cost at this pace, but I’m not letting a cup note slow throughput when the morning rush hits.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate wants a little handwritten note on cups when things are calm, so let’s make it feel like us—a smile or ‘enjoy’ is plenty. If the line builds or you’re juggling too much, take care of the people in front of you first.
managers.private_thought: I don’t want a tiny note to feel like one more box they have to tick, especially when they’re already making this place welcoming.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate wants a little note on cups when it’s quiet, so use your judgment if there’s an easy moment. Keep the line moving and take care of the customers.
managers.private_thought: Nobody checks this kiosk, and I’d rather keep the team focused on sales and service than make a thing of it.

managers.message_to_team: The memo says we need a mark on every cup while it’s calm, so please add a quick smiley or a short note and I’ll check in during the shift. If we get six or more waiting or we’re short-staffed, skip it and focus on the line.
managers.private_thought: I want to show I’m on top of this, but I hope the notes don’t slow us down or make the team feel micromanaged.

managers.message_to_team: If it's quiet, add a quick smiley or 'enjoy'—keep it simple and don't let it slow the line. If we get slammed or short, skip it and keep drinks moving.
managers.private_thought: At this gate, nobody's coming back for the handwriting, and I won't trade boarding-time speed for it.
